scr_ar_defining_transaction_allocations.purpose: Enables transaction allocations (in A/P configuration's Enable Functionality) and defines allocation rules that split a transaction across locations, departments or projects by fixed percentages.
scr_ar_defining_transaction_allocations.outcome: Reusable allocation rules available to A/R invoices, A/P invoices and journal entries.
scr_ar_defining_transaction_allocations.rootCause: Shared revenues and costs recur with the same split every month; defining the rule once guarantees each property receives its agreed share without recalculating each time.
scr_ar_defining_transaction_allocations.ifSkipped: Shared amounts are split by hand each month with inconsistent percentages.

scr_ar_where_to_apply_allocations.purpose: Explains where allocations can be applied — A/R invoice lines, A/P invoice lines, journal entries — and at what level.
scr_ar_where_to_apply_allocations.outcome: Users apply allocations in the right place for each shared transaction.
scr_ar_where_to_apply_allocations.rootCause: Applying allocations at the wrong level (header versus line) can split amounts that should stay with one property.
scr_ar_where_to_apply_allocations.ifSkipped: Allocations are applied inconsistently and property results are misstated.

scr_ar_adding_a_transaction_allocation.purpose: Creates a transaction allocation in General Ledger setup — name, dimensions and percentages — for use on invoices and entries.
scr_ar_adding_a_transaction_allocation.outcome: A new allocation rule ready to apply.
scr_ar_adding_a_transaction_allocation.rootCause: New shared arrangements (a shared amenity, a shared staff member billed to tenants) need a defined split before billing starts.
scr_ar_adding_a_transaction_allocation.ifSkipped: The first billings under a new arrangement are split ad hoc.
redFlags: Percentages not supported by an agreement or basis (units, square feet)

scr_ar_applying_an_allocation.purpose: Applies an existing allocation to an A/R invoice line so its amount is split automatically.
scr_ar_applying_an_allocation.outcome: Shared billings post to each property in the agreed proportions.
scr_ar_applying_an_allocation.rootCause: Applying a predefined rule removes manual calculation errors from recurring shared billings.
scr_ar_applying_an_allocation.ifSkipped: Shared revenue lands at one property and the other properties' NOI is understated.
redFlags: Wrong allocation chosen for the transaction

scr_ar_creating_an_allocation_split.purpose: Creates a one-off allocation split on a transaction when no predefined allocation fits.
scr_ar_creating_an_allocation_split.outcome: Unusual shared amounts are split correctly for that transaction only.
scr_ar_creating_an_allocation_split.rootCause: Some shared charges are one-time (a joint marketing event); an ad hoc split handles them without creating a permanent rule.
scr_ar_creating_an_allocation_split.ifSkipped: One-off shared amounts are recorded at a single property.
redFlags: Ad hoc splits used repeatedly instead of a defined rule

scr_ar_overriding_a_line_allocation.purpose: Overrides the default allocation on a specific invoice line when that line should be split differently or not at all.
scr_ar_overriding_a_line_allocation.outcome: Exceptions to the standard split handled line by line.
scr_ar_overriding_a_line_allocation.rootCause: A shared invoice may include one property-specific charge; overriding that line prevents it being spread to other properties.
scr_ar_overriding_a_line_allocation.ifSkipped: Property-specific charges are spread across properties.
redFlags: Frequent overrides of the same rule (rule is wrong)

scr_ar_restrictions_on_applying_allocati.purpose: Describes restrictions on allocations — for example with multi-currency transactions or entities that cannot transact with each other.
scr_ar_restrictions_on_applying_allocati.outcome: Users know when allocations cannot be used and what to do instead.
scr_ar_restrictions_on_applying_allocati.rootCause: Allocating across entities creates intercompany entries; restrictions prevent splits that would break entity boundaries or currency rules.
scr_ar_restrictions_on_applying_allocati.ifSkipped: Users attempt invalid allocations and create unbalanced entities.

scr_ar_intercompany_billing.purpose: Intercompany billing (available at top level) creates a matched pair of transactions — an A/R invoice in the billing entity and an A/P invoice in the billed entity — for charges between related entities.
scr_ar_intercompany_billing.outcome: Both sides of an affiliate charge are recorded at once and stay in balance.
scr_ar_intercompany_billing.rootCause: Management companies routinely charge properties for shared services (payroll, insurance, IT). Recording each side separately leads to mismatched Due To and Due From balances that never reconcile.
scr_ar_intercompany_billing.ifSkipped: Intercompany receivables and payables drift apart and consolidation eliminations fail.
redFlags: Intercompany balances not equal and opposite

scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_intercompany_.purpose: Views the list of intercompany billing transactions with their status and paired A/R and A/P invoices.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_intercompany_.outcome: Visibility of all affiliate billings and whether they are settled.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_intercompany_.rootCause: Unsettled intercompany balances accumulate quietly; reviewing the list drives monthly settlement.
scr_ar_viewing_the_list_of_intercompany_.ifSkipped: Affiliate balances grow unsettled and look like undisclosed loans between entities.

scr_ar_intercompany_billing_list.purpose: Lists intercompany billing records with actions to add, edit, view, duplicate and delete.
scr_ar_intercompany_billing_list.outcome: A managed register of affiliate charges.
scr_ar_intercompany_billing_list.rootCause: A single register of affiliate charges supports monthly intercompany reconciliation and owner scrutiny of related-party charges.
scr_ar_intercompany_billing_list.ifSkipped: Related-party charges are hard to review and reconcile.

scr_ar_creating_an_intercompany_bill.purpose: Creates an intercompany bill — billing entity, billed entity, lines, amounts — saved as draft or posted to generate both sides.
scr_ar_creating_an_intercompany_bill.outcome: Matched A/R and A/P records between affiliates.
scr_ar_creating_an_intercompany_bill.rootCause: Creating both sides from one entry guarantees they match in amount, date and description.
scr_ar_creating_an_intercompany_bill.ifSkipped: Affiliate charges are recorded on one side only.
redFlags: Charges not supported by the management agreement

scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_intercompany_.purpose: Edits an intercompany billing while it is still a draft, or views a posted one, to confirm the billing entity, billed entity, lines and amounts match the agreed charge.
scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_intercompany_.outcome: Affiliate charges corrected before posting or reviewed afterwards.
scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_intercompany_.rootCause: Correcting before posting keeps both sides aligned; after posting, reversal is needed.
scr_ar_editing_and_viewing_intercompany_.ifSkipped: Errors are posted to both entities and must be reversed on both sides.
redFlags: Edits after one side was paid

scr_ar_paying_an_intercompany_invoice.purpose: Pays the A/P side of an intercompany invoice from the billed entity's bank account, settling the affiliate charge in cash.
scr_ar_paying_an_intercompany_invoice.outcome: The affiliate charge is settled in cash.
scr_ar_paying_an_intercompany_invoice.rootCause: Owners expect intercompany balances to be settled regularly; long-open balances look like undisclosed loans between entities.
scr_ar_paying_an_intercompany_invoice.ifSkipped: Intercompany balances accumulate and raise related-party questions.
redFlags: Payments not matched on the receiving side

scr_ar_applying_a_payment_to_an_intercom.purpose: Applies the payment received by the billing entity to the A/R side of an intercompany bill, so both entities show the charge as settled.
scr_ar_applying_a_payment_to_an_intercom.outcome: Both sides of the affiliate charge show as settled.
scr_ar_applying_a_payment_to_an_intercom.rootCause: If the payment is recorded on one side only, balances diverge and the intercompany reconciliation fails.
scr_ar_applying_a_payment_to_an_intercom.ifSkipped: The receivable stays open after payment and balances do not match.

scr_ar_duplicating_an_intercompany_billi.purpose: Copies an existing intercompany bill for a recurring affiliate charge — for example the next month's shared payroll billing.
scr_ar_duplicating_an_intercompany_billi.rootCause: Affiliate charges often repeat monthly with similar lines; copying keeps coding consistent.
scr_ar_duplicating_an_intercompany_billi.ifSkipped: Recurring charges are rebuilt with inconsistent coding.
redFlags: Copies with last month's amounts unchanged

scr_ar_deleting_an_intercompany_billing_.purpose: Deletes a draft intercompany billing entered in error — for example a shared-payroll charge keyed twice — before it posts to either entity.
scr_ar_deleting_an_intercompany_billing_.outcome: Erroneous affiliate charges removed before posting.
scr_ar_deleting_an_intercompany_billing_.rootCause: Duplicate affiliate charges inflate both entities' balances and must be removed before they post to either side.
scr_ar_deleting_an_intercompany_billing_.ifSkipped: Duplicate charges post to both entities.

scr_ar_intercompany_billing_page.purpose: The page for adding or changing an intercompany billing — entities, lines and the generated A/R and A/P invoice information.
scr_ar_intercompany_billing_page.outcome: Complete definition of an affiliate charge and both sides it creates.
scr_ar_intercompany_billing_page.rootCause: Seeing the A/R and A/P sides on one page before posting is what guarantees the two entities record identical amounts, dates and descriptions, which is required for intercompany balances to eliminate on consolidation.
scr_ar_intercompany_billing_page.ifSkipped: Mismatched sides are posted and the intercompany reconciliation fails.
redFlags: Different descriptions on the two sides

scr_ar_inter_company_bill_back.purpose: The inter-company bill-back feature automatically creates an A/R invoice to recover a cost when an A/P invoice is recorded for an expense belonging to another entity.
scr_ar_inter_company_bill_back.outcome: Costs paid on behalf of affiliates are billed back automatically.
scr_ar_inter_company_bill_back.rootCause: Management companies frequently pay vendors on behalf of properties (or vice versa). Without automation, bill-backs are forgotten and the paying entity absorbs the cost.
scr_ar_inter_company_bill_back.ifSkipped: Costs paid on behalf of affiliates are never recovered.
redFlags: Costs paid for affiliates without bill-backs

scr_ar_what_does_inter_company_bill_back.purpose: Explains how bill-back works: an A/P invoice flagged for bill-back generates a corresponding A/R invoice to the responsible entity, optionally with markup.
scr_ar_what_does_inter_company_bill_back.outcome: Users understand the automatic link between payable and recovery.
scr_ar_what_does_inter_company_bill_back.rootCause: Understanding the mechanism helps accountants flag the right invoices and reconcile the resulting receivables.
scr_ar_what_does_inter_company_bill_back.ifSkipped: Invoices are not flagged and recoveries are missed.

scr_ar_bill_back_feature_configuration_w.purpose: The configuration workflow for bill-back — enabling the feature, mapping accounts and setting customer relationships between entities.
scr_ar_bill_back_feature_configuration_w.outcome: Bill-back produces correct receivables in the right entities.
scr_ar_bill_back_feature_configuration_w.rootCause: Bill-back depends on account and customer mappings; incomplete configuration produces invoices to the wrong entity or account.
scr_ar_bill_back_feature_configuration_w.ifSkipped: Bill-backs are created incorrectly or not at all.

scr_ar_using_the_inter_company_bill_back.purpose: Uses the bill-back workflow day to day — flagging A/P invoices for bill-back and reviewing generated A/R invoices.
scr_ar_using_the_inter_company_bill_back.outcome: Routine recovery of costs paid for other entities.
scr_ar_using_the_inter_company_bill_back.rootCause: Consistent use ensures every cost paid for another entity is recovered in the same period.
scr_ar_using_the_inter_company_bill_back.ifSkipped: Costs paid on behalf of affiliates are recovered late or never.
redFlags: Bill-backs generated in a later period than the cost

scr_ar_managing_inter_company_bill_back_.purpose: Manages bill-back invoices — creating, viewing, and disabling bill-back transactions.
scr_ar_managing_inter_company_bill_back_.rootCause: Bill-back receivables must be followed to collection like any other receivable, and incorrect ones removed.
scr_ar_managing_inter_company_bill_back_.ifSkipped: Bill-back receivables from affiliates go uncollected and age on the balance sheet.

scr_ar_creating_a_bill_back_invoice.purpose: Creates a bill-back invoice from an A/P invoice so the responsible entity is billed for the cost.
scr_ar_creating_a_bill_back_invoice.outcome: A receivable from the affiliate matching the cost paid.
scr_ar_creating_a_bill_back_invoice.rootCause: Linking the bill-back to the original A/P invoice provides support and prevents double billing.
scr_ar_creating_a_bill_back_invoice.ifSkipped: Costs are not recovered or recovered twice.

scr_ar_viewing_an_a_p_invoice_created_wi.purpose: Views the A/P invoice created on the billed entity's side by the bill-back feature.
scr_ar_viewing_an_a_p_invoice_created_wi.outcome: The payable side of the bill-back is visible for approval and payment.
scr_ar_viewing_an_a_p_invoice_created_wi.rootCause: The receiving entity must approve and pay the bill-back; seeing it confirms both sides exist.

scr_ar_disabling_inter_company_bill_back.purpose: Disables bill-back for transactions that should not be recovered — for example costs the management company agreed to absorb.
scr_ar_disabling_inter_company_bill_back.rootCause: Some costs are non-reimbursable under the management agreement; disabling bill-back prevents billing owners for them.
scr_ar_disabling_inter_company_bill_back.ifSkipped: Owners are billed for non-reimbursable costs.

scr_ar_payments.purpose: Chapter on A/R payments — receiving and applying customer payments and advances, deposits, adjustments and write-offs.
scr_ar_payments.outcome: A complete process for turning receivables into cash.
scr_ar_payments.rootCause: Collections, application, deposit and write-off must follow a consistent process for the aging and cash to be reliable.
scr_ar_payments.ifSkipped: Receipts are handled inconsistently and aging becomes unreliable.

scr_ar_payments_2.purpose: Section on receiving customer payments and applying them to invoices, including overpayments, credits and other receipts.
scr_ar_payments_2.outcome: Customer payments recorded against the right invoices.
scr_ar_payments_2.rootCause: Correct application determines what remains outstanding and what is chased; misapplication creates false delinquency.
scr_ar_payments_2.ifSkipped: Customers are chased for invoices they have already paid.

scr_ar_receiving_payments_q_and_a.purpose: Answers common questions about receiving payments — how to enter unapplied payments, partial payments, overpayments and payments without an invoice.
scr_ar_receiving_payments_q_and_a.rootCause: Unusual receipts are where most application errors happen; clear answers reduce misapplied cash.

scr_ar_select_invoices_for_payment_page.purpose: The page used to receive a payment and select which open invoices it pays, with amounts applied per invoice.
scr_ar_select_invoices_for_payment_page.outcome: Each receipt is matched to specific invoices.
scr_ar_select_invoices_for_payment_page.rootCause: Commercial tenants often pay several invoices with one check and specify which; applying accordingly keeps both sides' records aligned.
scr_ar_select_invoices_for_payment_page.ifSkipped: Applications differ from the customer's remittance and disputes follow.

scr_ar_receiving_a_payment_2.purpose: Records a customer check or electronic payment, entering payer, amount, reference and deposit account before applying it to invoices.
scr_ar_receiving_a_payment_2.outcome: The receipt is recorded and ready for deposit and application.
scr_ar_receiving_a_payment_2.rootCause: Recording the check number and payer precisely allows matching to the bank deposit and resolving any dispute.
scr_ar_receiving_a_payment_2.ifSkipped: Receipts cannot be traced to bank deposits or resolved in disputes.

scr_ar_entering_an_overpayment.purpose: Records a payment larger than the amount due, leaving the excess as a customer credit.
scr_ar_entering_an_overpayment.outcome: Overpayments are held as credits owed to the customer, not taken to income.
scr_ar_entering_an_overpayment.rootCause: Overpaid amounts belong to the customer until applied or refunded; recording them as income overstates revenue and creates unclaimed property exposure.
scr_ar_entering_an_overpayment.ifSkipped: Overpayments are hidden in income and never refunded.

scr_ar_refunding_an_overpayment.purpose: Refunds a customer's overpayment or credit balance by creating a refund through A/P, clearing the credit from the customer's account.
scr_ar_refunding_an_overpayment.outcome: Customer credits are returned and cleared.
scr_ar_refunding_an_overpayment.rootCause: Credits left unrefunded eventually become unclaimed property owed to the state; refunding promptly clears the liability.
scr_ar_refunding_an_overpayment.ifSkipped: Credit balances age into escheat obligations.
redFlags: Refunds to different payees than the original payer

scr_ar_applying_a_credit_memo_to_an_invo.purpose: Applies a customer's credit memo (from a returned charge or billing correction) against an open invoice.
scr_ar_applying_a_credit_memo_to_an_invo.outcome: Credits reduce open invoices instead of sitting separately.
scr_ar_applying_a_credit_memo_to_an_invo.rootCause: Unapplied credits make both the invoice and the credit look open, overstating receivables and liabilities.
scr_ar_applying_a_credit_memo_to_an_invo.ifSkipped: Aging shows offsetting open items and customers dispute balances.
redFlags: Credits applied to the wrong customer's invoices

scr_ar_applying_credits_without_recordin.purpose: Applies existing credits to invoices without a new payment, for example matching an old overpayment to this month's invoice.
scr_ar_applying_credits_without_recordin.outcome: Credits and invoices net off cleanly.
scr_ar_applying_credits_without_recordin.rootCause: Credits often need to be applied without any cash changing hands; this path clears both items.
scr_ar_applying_credits_without_recordin.ifSkipped: Credits and invoices both remain open, overstating the aging.

scr_ar_applying_credits_as_you_record_a_.purpose: Applies available credits while recording a new payment, so the payment plus credits settle the selected invoices.
scr_ar_applying_credits_as_you_record_a_.outcome: Payment and credits combined to settle invoices in one step.
scr_ar_applying_credits_as_you_record_a_.rootCause: Customers often short-pay by the amount of credits they expect to be applied; applying credits at receipt matches their remittance.
scr_ar_applying_credits_as_you_record_a_.ifSkipped: Short payments leave invoices partially open while credits remain unused.
redFlags: Credits applied that the customer did not claim

scr_ar_changing_the_amount_credited_afte.purpose: Changes how much of a credit was applied after application, where configuration allows.
scr_ar_changing_the_amount_credited_afte.outcome: Credit applications corrected without reversing payments.
scr_ar_changing_the_amount_credited_afte.rootCause: Applying the wrong credit amount is a common error; correcting it directly avoids reversing and re-entering the payment.
scr_ar_changing_the_amount_credited_afte.ifSkipped: Errors persist or payments are reversed unnecessarily.

scr_ar_receiving_other_payments.purpose: Records other payment types — manual deposits and payments not tied to specific invoices — through the Receive a Payment page.
scr_ar_receiving_other_payments.outcome: Unusual receipts are recorded in A/R rather than outside it.
scr_ar_receiving_other_payments.rootCause: Not every customer receipt matches an invoice (deposits, prepayments); recording them in A/R keeps the customer ledger complete.
scr_ar_receiving_other_payments.ifSkipped: Customer receipts are recorded elsewhere and the ledger is incomplete.

scr_ar_applying_a_payment_to_an_invoice.purpose: Applies a recorded customer payment to one or more open invoices so they show as paid and the customer's balance is reduced.
scr_ar_applying_a_payment_to_an_invoice.outcome: Invoices marked paid and aging reduced.
scr_ar_applying_a_payment_to_an_invoice.rootCause: A payment recorded but not applied leaves both an open invoice and an unapplied credit, overstating the customer's delinquency.
scr_ar_applying_a_payment_to_an_invoice.ifSkipped: Customers look delinquent while holding unapplied payments.
redFlags: Unapplied payments older than one month

scr_ar_turning_off_auto_payment_suggesti.purpose: Turns off automatic payment application suggestions so users apply payments manually.
scr_ar_turning_off_auto_payment_suggesti.outcome: Payments are applied only as the customer remitted.
scr_ar_turning_off_auto_payment_suggesti.rootCause: Auto-suggestions apply to the oldest invoice by default, which may contradict the customer's remittance and cause disputes.
scr_ar_turning_off_auto_payment_suggesti.ifSkipped: Payments are applied against customer instructions.

scr_ar_posted_payments_list_accounts_rec.purpose: Lists posted customer payments with payer, date, amount, deposit status and application.
scr_ar_posted_payments_list_accounts_rec.outcome: A register of collections for review and reconciliation.
scr_ar_posted_payments_list_accounts_rec.rootCause: Posted payments must tie to deposits and bank credits; the list supports that matching and investigation of disputes.
scr_ar_posted_payments_list_accounts_rec.ifSkipped: Payments cannot be efficiently matched to deposits.
redFlags: Posted payments not yet deposited after several days

scr_ar_viewing_a_list_of_posted_payments.purpose: Opens the posted payments list and filters it by customer, date range or amount to find specific receipts — typically to answer a customer's 'did you receive our payment?' inquiry.
scr_ar_viewing_a_list_of_posted_payments.rootCause: Customer inquiries ('did you receive our payment?') require locating payments quickly.
scr_ar_viewing_a_list_of_posted_payments.ifSkipped: Payment inquiries go unanswered or take too long.
redFlags: Duplicate payments from the same customer

scr_ar_viewing_posted_payments.purpose: Views a posted customer payment's details — payer, method, reference, invoices applied and deposit — to resolve disputes or misapplications.
scr_ar_viewing_posted_payments.outcome: The full record of how one receipt was handled.
scr_ar_viewing_posted_payments.rootCause: Resolving disputes and misapplications requires seeing exactly how a payment was applied.
scr_ar_viewing_posted_payments.ifSkipped: Misapplied payments go unnoticed and disputes drag on.
redFlags: Payments applied to another customer's invoice

scr_ar_reversing_posted_payments.purpose: Reverses a posted customer payment from Search & Find — for a returned check or a payment applied to the wrong customer.
scr_ar_reversing_posted_payments.outcome: The payment's effect is undone and the invoices reopen.
scr_ar_reversing_posted_payments.rootCause: Returned or misapplied payments must be undone with a trail so the customer balance and cash are correct.
scr_ar_reversing_posted_payments.ifSkipped: Returned payments stay credited and A/R is understated.

scr_ar_reversing_a_payment_from_the_rece.purpose: Reverses a customer payment directly from the Receipts Register report while reviewing receipts, without navigating to the payment record.
scr_ar_reversing_a_payment_from_the_rece.outcome: Payments reversed from the register while reviewing receipts.
scr_ar_reversing_a_payment_from_the_rece.rootCause: Errors are often spotted while reviewing the register; reversing from there saves navigating to the payment.
scr_ar_reversing_a_payment_from_the_rece.ifSkipped: Errors spotted in review are not corrected promptly.

scr_ar_how_to_access_the_invoice_again_t.purpose: Explains how to reopen an invoice after reversing a misapplied payment so the correct payment can be applied.
scr_ar_how_to_access_the_invoice_again_t.rootCause: After reversal, the invoice must be located again and the right payment applied; missing this step leaves the invoice open.
scr_ar_how_to_access_the_invoice_again_t.ifSkipped: Invoices stay open after a reversal and customers are chased.
